text.p: Belgian photo finishing group Spector NV said on Friday it would issue 734,889 reduced withholding tax (VVPR) shares to the public at a price of 1,865 francs each.
Under the terms of the offer, which runs from October 7 to 21, four new shares would be issued for every nine presently held, Spector said.
The issue is part of Spector's 2.75 billion Belgian franc capital increase announced last month to pay for recent acquisitions in Germany, France, Hungary, Switzerland and Belgium.

The company is issuing a total of 1,475,977 new shares, 50.2 percent of which have been allocated to Porst Holding AG, which following the recent acquisitions has become one of Spector's major shareholders.
The capital increase will bring Spector's issued capital to 4,796,925 shares, it said.
The issue is being joint led by banks ASLK-CGER and Paribas Belgium. Spector NV is Europe's leading independent photo finishing group.
Last month Spector acquired Interdiscount France and the activities of Porst Holding AG.
Spector managing director Tonny Van Doorslaer declined on Friday to estimate full-year 1996 group net profit, saying it was "too early to forecast".

However, Bank Paribas Belgium is forecasting lower 1996 group net profit of 110 million francs due to the acquisitions and lower sales, before a sharp rise in 1997 to 702 million francs due to synergies from the group's restructuring.
Group net profit in 1995 and 1994 was 235 million francs and 205 million francs respectively.
